items.event_time_ist: Oct 11, 2026 (Sunday morning US time)
items.summary: Trump posted on Truth Social that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an immediate 'energy ceasefire' — 'Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!' — giving no scope, duration or verification detail. It is his second such declaration: he made a near-identical claim on Sept 14, which Putin rebuffed (per WSJ), after which strikes on energy targets continued. The announcement came days after the Oct 9 US-Russia deal suspending sanctions to allow up to 4.8M tonnes of Russian diesel onto world markets (Treasury licence running to Apr 7, 2027); Trump has blamed Ukrainian refinery strikes for the US diesel-price spike ($6.28/gal, AAA) ahead of the midterms.
items.title: Trump announces immediate 'energy ceasefire' between Russia and Ukraine

items.summary: Zelensky said the announcement came as news to him — telling Axios it caught Kyiv off guard — but that Ukraine is ready to accept an energy ceasefire if Russia agrees, and is awaiting details on when it begins. After the announcement he spoke with Canadian PM Mark Carney, Finnish President Alexander Stubb and NATO chief Mark Rutte. At the Warsaw Security Forum on Monday (via video link) he said Ukraine would abide if Russia does, noting Russian refineries were not burning the previous night — while Russia struck Ukrainian energy targets.
items.title: Zelensky says ceasefire was news to Kyiv, but Ukraine will abide if Russia does

items.event_time_ist: Night of Oct 11 into morning of Oct 12, 2026
items.summary: Zelensky said Russia hit at least six energy targets in overnight and morning strikes across Ukraine, showing Moscow has no interest in the energy ceasefire. Targets included a Kharkiv power plant struck Sunday night in an attack that killed 3 and wounded 9 (including children), a gas production facility hit by a jet-powered Shahed drone, and a gas facility plus a petrol station hit by drones; a Kyiv power plant was also reported struck. The Kremlin has not confirmed any ceasefire agreement; spokesman Peskov said only that 'contacts are ongoing'.
items.title: Russia keeps hitting Ukrainian energy targets despite ceasefire claim

items.summary: Ukraine's European allies voiced scepticism of the purported energy ceasefire, spoke strongly in support of Kyiv, and approved the largest set of EU sanctions since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.
items.title: EU approves its largest sanctions package since the 2022 invasion

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, 2026 (reported Oct 12)
items.summary: Amid a strained relationship between the two leaders, Trump called on Ukrainians to remove Zelensky through an election — an unusually severe exchange as Trump pushes his ceasefire narrative while Zelensky criticised the US diesel deal with Russia as reversing years of Western isolation policy.
items.title: Trump publicly calls on Ukrainians to unseat Zelensky in an election

items.summary: Zelensky told ABC's 'This Week' on Sunday (Oct 11) to 'tell Putin, give us two months, 60 days of total ceasefire' so Ukraine can hold presidential elections (wartime elections are banned under Ukrainian law). At Monday's briefing, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov rejected the idea, saying Russia does not want a ceasefire but a long-term peace deal — though he added that Putin, as commander-in-chief, would order no attacks on election day itself if Kyiv genuinely wants elections. On Trump's 'energy ceasefire,' Peskov said discussions were continuing, declined to say whether it would apply only to oil refineries, and said further details would be announced in due course. Image is a representative photo of the Kremlin, Moscow — not the briefing itself.
items.title: Kremlin rejects Zelensky's 60-day ceasefire-for-elections proposal; says energy-ceasefire talks continue but scope undisclosed

items.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said Monday (Oct 12) that Moscow will not be swayed by ceasefire assurances: 'I do not believe he has earned such a respite, nor do I think we will once again fall for assurances and promises.' Lavrov said Kyiv would use any pause to regroup and rearm with European weapons — a markedly harder Kremlin rejection than spokesman Peskov's 'discussions continue' line from the same day. Image is a representative Reuters photo of Lavrov at the Foreign Ministry — not Monday's video address.
items.title: Lavrov flatly rejects energy ceasefire: Ukraine doesn't 'deserve a respite'

items.summary: In a Truth Social post Monday (Oct 12), Trump defended his Russian diesel import deal amid bipartisan backlash — seven senators, including four Republicans, demanded he reverse course, warning it violates the 2022 Russian energy import ban. 'The European Union paid Russia 250 Billion Dollars for Energy, and the Fake News Media doesn't want to get near that story. I made the right choice for the American People,' Trump wrote, accusing Europe of continuing to buy Russian oil and gas. Image is a representative photo of Trump at the White House briefing podium — not the post itself.
items.title: Trump defends Russian diesel deal on Truth Social, accuses Europe of buying Russian oil

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, 2026, ~11:46 AM IST (morning, per AzerNews timestamp)
items.source_name: Axios (via AzerNews); TASS (via topwar.ru); Ian Bremmer / GZERO Media
items.summary: Axios reported that Trump's special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner postponed a planned trip to Moscow because Washington has no clear read on whether Kyiv and EU allies will back a new US proposal - a halt to attacks on energy infrastructure (oil refineries) as a first step, followed by broader peace talks. TASS sources stressed the trip is not cancelled and could happen within ~2 weeks once Kyiv's position is clear. Eurasia Group's Ian Bremmer separately tied the envoys' delayed Moscow travel to the energy ceasefire's uncertain status 24 hours after Trump's announcement. (Image: representative photo of US envoy Steve Witkoff.)
items.title: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner postpone planned Moscow trip over unclear Kyiv/EU position on US ceasefire proposal

items.event_time_ist: Overnight of Oct 11 into Oct 12, 2026
items.summary: After the overnight Oct 11-12 strikes, a Russian strike destroyed power grids in Izyum, leaving the city in blackout (per Ukraine's Ukrinform). State grid operator Ukrenergo reported fresh power cuts across the Kharkiv, Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia regions, while energy and railway infrastructure in western Ukraine was also targeted overnight into Monday, Oct 12.
items.title: Russian strike destroys power grids in Izyum; Ukrenergo cuts power in Kharkiv, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia

items.event_time_ist: Monday, Oct 12, 2026 (White House, before Ohio rally)
items.summary: Asked at the White House to condemn Russia's strikes on Ukraine, President Trump declined - 'I'd have to look at it and see, because there's been violations on both sides' - and claimed 'Putin wants to make a deal more than Zelensky,' pressing Zelensky to 'focus on making a deal.'
items.title: Trump at the White House refuses to condemn Russian strikes: 'violations on both sides'

items.event_time_ist: Monday, Oct 12, 2026 (Kyiv local)
items.summary: A Monday-evening strike on a 25-story residential building in Kyiv's Darnitskyi district killed 2 and injured 9 (Reuters). Near Kramatorsk, a house in Cherkaske was hit - 3 killed including a 13-year-old girl - with Donetsk admin head Vadym Filashkin alleging cluster munitions in 'a deliberate attempt' to maximize civilian casualties. In Kharkiv a collapsed building entrance injured 5, one person died in a Lozova drone attack, and one each near Fastiv and in Dnipro.
items.title: Monday's civilian toll: Kyiv high-rise hit, family killed near Kramatorsk, more struck in Kharkiv, Lozova, Fastiv, Dnipro

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, 2026 (Monday trading session)
items.title: Crude prices slip on 'energy ceasefire' hopes; IEA chief urges member states to weigh diesel releases
items.summary: Oil fell Monday on expectations of more Russian supplies after Trump's Sunday 'energy ceasefire' claim and the Friday US-Russia diesel deal. Brent crude dropped ~1.3% to around $103.35-103.40/bbl and WTI ~1.4-1.6% to about $90.40-90.60/bbl, while ICE gasoil fell 3% to $1,436/ton after Russia promised 300,000 tons of diesel immediately plus 500,000 tons in November. IEA executive director Fatih Birol urged member countries Sunday to consider whether extra diesel releases might be needed and to accelerate promised supplies, with a focus on diesel. Analysts cautioned the pullback would stay limited without evidence the ceasefire holds; Middle East conflict risk kept Brent above $100.

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, 2026 (report published; meeting held Friday Oct 9)
items.summary: Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner told Ukrainian officials in a meeting in Miami on Friday that the US-Russia diesel deal (2.25M+ barrels) is part of a bid to draw Russia back to negotiations after the failure of previous efforts — the deal could 'soften' Moscow's position and help restart trilateral talks. The envoys said Putin is not prepared to negotiate an end to the war; a person close to the Kremlin said Putin will only return to the table when 'he gets the remaining 11% of Donbas.' Kushner reiterated the US demand that Ukraine stop striking Russian refineries ('See, the Ukrainians stopped striking and we gave you this deal. Now it's your turn to do something'), stressing the US had made the request several times. The Ukrainians were skeptical of using business deals to appease Russia, left without agreeing to anything formally, but signaled willingness to accept an energy ceasefire so long as Russia does. The meeting also touched on security guarantees, reconstruction funds and World Bank involvement.
items.title: Reuters: US meant diesel deal as lure to 'soften' Moscow and restart trilateral talks; Kushner pressed Kyiv again on refinery strikes

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12-13, 2026 (strikes Monday and overnight; claims reported Oct 13)
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry claimed Monday drone strikes hit three cargo vessels it alleged were transporting military or dual-use cargo to Black Sea ports — two dry cargo ships bound for Odesa struck at sea and one for Mykolaiv — plus port infrastructure and a Nova Poshta logistics center in Ternivka (Mykolaiv region) that it said stored dual-use goods for Ukraine's armed forces. A Tuesday briefing listed further overnight targets: a workshop at the Pulp Mill Print facility in Kyiv (said to produce missiles and long-range drones), the Darnytsia locomotive depot (rolling stock used for military cargo), a UAV warehouse in Meshkovo-Pohorelove, and a dry cargo vessel in the Bug estuary. Reuters could not independently verify the claims; no Ukrainian response reported. None of the claimed targets were energy facilities.
items.title: Russia's Defence Ministry claims drone strikes on 3 cargo ships and logistics targets in Odesa/Mykolaiv and Kyiv regions

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, 2026 (Novak's Rossiya-24 interview aired Monday; Reuters published Oct 12, 2026)
items.summary: On Monday Oct 12, Deputy PM Alexander Novak told Rossiya-24 that Russia can return diesel exports to 3.0-3.5M metric tons per month by year-end - above the roughly 4.8M-ton schedule Trump outlined Friday under the US-Russia deal - saying global diesel prices had already fallen about 5-6%. He said Moscow is discussing supplies with Washington through energy departments and companies, and noted the government cleared 500,000 tons of diesel for export after the Friday Putin-Trump call.
items.title: Russia says diesel exports could exceed Trump's outlined volumes; Novak targets 3-3.5M tons/month by year-end

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, 2026 (afternoon Berlin time)
items.title: Merz: Trump's Russian diesel deal 'out of the question' for Europe
items.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said at a Berlin press conference Monday that the US-brokered arrangement for Russian diesel exports is 'out of the question' for Germany and Europe; Berlin will keep its sanctions on Moscow and continue supporting Ukraine. Merz argued Russia negotiates 'seriously' only under pressure, noted Russia kept hitting Ukraine's civilian energy infrastructure after Trump's 'energy ceasefire' claim, and said EU leaders will coordinate strategy at the Brussels summit Thursday-Friday.

items.event_time_ist: Evening, Oct 12, 2026
items.title: Merz-Zelensky call: responsibility for energy ceasefire 'rests with Russia'
items.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz held a telephone call with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday evening. Zelensky briefed him on the weekend's massive Russian aerial attacks on civilian areas and energy infrastructure; Merz reaffirmed Germany's solidarity, and both agreed the responsibility for establishing a ceasefire over all energy infrastructure now rests with Russia. They also agreed to keep coordinating closely with European and transatlantic partners on peace efforts.
items.source_name: German government (spokesman Stefan Kornelius) via Osna.FM

items.event_time_ist: Overnight of Oct 12 into Oct 13, 2026 (Russia's Defence Ministry Tuesday summary; Kremlin comment Tuesday Oct 13)
items.summary: Reuters (Kyiv, Oct 13) reports Russia's Defence Ministry made no mention of Ukrainian energy facilities in its daily summary of overnight strikes - the first night since Trump's Sunday 'energy ceasefire' announcement with no reported energy targeting. Overnight attacks instead hit transport and logistics: ballistic missiles and drones struck Kyiv transport and warehouse facilities (Dniprovskyi, Desnianskyi). One missile landed just over a kilometre from a plant providing heating to much of Lviv in the west. The Kremlin (Peskov) on Tuesday still refused to confirm the ceasefire, saying only that 'contacts are continuing' and declining further details. Zelensky counters that Russia has continued hitting energy and critical infrastructure over the two days.
items.title: Russia claims no energy targets hit overnight Tuesday - first night since Trump's 'truce'

items.event_time_ist: Tuesday Oct 13, 2026 (Zelensky statement on overnight Oct 12-13 attacks)
items.source_name: Zelensky statement (via AAP/Reuters, AnewZ live blog)
items.summary: Zelensky said Tuesday that since Monday evening Russia has attacked Ukraine with more than a hundred weapons - jet-powered drones, loitering munitions and ballistic missiles. A strike destroyed a residential building in Kharkiv, killing 4; 41 people were injured in Kharkiv in a single evening. A ballistic-missile strike on Kyiv hit civilian infrastructure, and Zelensky complained Ukraine received no early warning from partners about the launch - a new dig at the US intelligence-sharing threat. He said Ukraine has not struck Russian refineries or the energy sector at all for the two days since Trump's announcement, while Russia 'did not heed the American President' and kept hitting energy facilities and critical infrastructure; 19 regions came under attack in two days. He added Ukraine is ready for reciprocal steps toward de-escalation. Kyiv Post's updated overnight report corroborates the toll: two women killed in Kyiv, four killed in Kharkiv.
items.title: Zelensky: >100 Russian weapons overnight; 4 killed in Kharkiv; Ukraine has held off refinery strikes for two days

items.event_time_ist: Tuesday Oct 13, 2026 (at the Warsaw Security Forum; forum-day, Warsaw time)
items.source_name: The London Weekly; PA wire (via Clacton Gazette)
items.summary: At the Warsaw Security Forum on Tuesday Oct 13, UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband urged European partners to back an energy ceasefire, saying the idea 'should be taken seriously' because 'in the last week alone we've seen 200 Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure' (Foreign Office figures; 1,450 bombs and 1,600 drones in the same period). He acknowledged a 'very difficult few days' in relations with Washington after Trump's diesel deal and his calls for Zelensky's removal, praised Zelensky's 'extraordinary leadership,' and said: 'let us seek with President Trump to hold Putin to this full energy ceasefire.' He also met Polish FM Sikorski and said the UK would move with the EU on using frozen Russian assets if the bloc agrees. Catch-up: earlier runs missed this forum-day item.
items.title: UK's Miliband urges European allies to back energy ceasefire at Warsaw Security Forum; cites 200 Russian energy-infra attacks in a week

items.event_time_ist: Sunday Oct 11, 2026 (PMO readout after the Carney-Zelensky call)
items.summary: After a Sunday Oct 11 call with Zelensky, Canadian PM Mark Carney's office said Trump's US-Russia diesel agreement 'is in direct opposition to the efforts of Ukraine, Canada, and our allies to create peace and stability in Europe' and 'will provide additional revenue for Russia and help finance its illegal, unjustifiable war against Ukraine'; Carney said Canada remains willing to expand its Russia sanctions. On the same day he also thanked Trump for 'his leadership toward securing an energy ceasefire.' Catch-up: this Oct 11 PMO statement was missed by all earlier runs.
items.title: Canada's Carney publicly slammed Trump's diesel deal with Russia (Oct 11 PMO statement, catch-up)

items.event_time_ist: Morning of Tuesday Oct 13, 2026 (Washington, DC)
items.title: Trump shrugs at Russian strikes after ceasefire: asked if upset Putin hit energy targets, answers 'we'll see… they're both a little bit off'
items.summary: Asked by Scripps News on Tuesday morning whether he was upset that Vladimir Putin struck energy targets after the weekend 'energy ceasefire' announcement, Trump answered 'we'll see… they're both a little bit off,' adding 'bottom line, it's all gonna work out… you know why… it always does.' The noncommittal reply — his first on-camera comment Tuesday on the continued strikes — offered no condemnation of Russia and no new action; it follows Monday's 'violations on both sides' line and repeated insistence the ceasefire exists because he said so.

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, 2026 (announced by Macron Monday evening; Reuters wire Tuesday Oct 13)
items.summary: The French Navy intercepted and boarded the oil tanker MT DF Peak (IMO 9341067, ex-Kaliningrad, Benin-flagged) about 450 nautical miles south of Réunion on Monday Oct 12 — the fifth French shadow-fleet interception this year. President Macron posted boarding footage on X, saying France is "determined to combat the ghost fleet" over its suspected false flag and illicit fuel transport. The vessel is under escort to Réunion for investigation. Russia's embassy in France (via RIA, Tuesday) called the seizure "piracy" and a blatant violation of international law, saying France did not notify it and it is checking whether Russian nationals are aboard. USNI notes Putin threatened symmetrical retaliatory actions on Oct 1.
items.title: France seizes suspected Russian shadow-fleet tanker DF Peak; Moscow calls it "piracy"

items.event_time_ist: Oct 13, 2026 (Tuesday, reported ~8:43 AM PDT)
items.summary: President Trump told reporters Tuesday that the United States continues to share intelligence with Ukraine — "We are helping them, and we are sharing intel" — after FT/CNN reported Monday that US officials had warned Kyiv intel assistance (and, per NY Post, weapons deliveries to Europe) would stop unless Ukraine reined in its long-range strikes on Russian refineries. FM Sybiha had earlier Tuesday said US-Ukrainian intelligence cooperation continues. Trump also defended the Russian diesel deal, saying the fuel is "being released into the world... not to us," sidestepped whether Russia could use the proceeds to buy more bombs, and claimed both Putin and Zelensky "want the war to end" but "there is a lot of hatred between the two of them."
items.title: Trump says US is still sharing intelligence with Ukraine, denies cutoff threat

items.event_time_ist: morning of Oct 13, 2026 (Kyiv time); casualty count updated through midday
items.title: Russian drone strikes hit western Ukraine Tuesday morning: educational institution in Rivne (up to 25 injured), homes near Lviv
items.summary: Tuesday morning Oct 13 (Kyiv time), Russian drones struck civilian targets in western Ukraine amid the disputed 'energy ceasefire.' A drone hit an educational institution in central Rivne: regional governor Oleksandr Koval reported injuries rising from 10 at 11:37 a.m. local to 14 by 11:50 a.m., one in serious condition; Ukraine's national police later put the toll at 20-25 injured, 2 in intensive care, with the building badly damaged (cars, a mobile cafe and adjacent buildings also damaged). Separately, a downed Russian drone fell on a residential building in the village of Murovane near Lviv during an air-raid alert (jet drones were recorded over Lviv region after 5 a.m.); three houses caught fire and several cars were damaged, no casualties reported per the Lviv regional administration. Strikes continue across Ukraine despite the claimed truce.

items.event_time_ist: Night of Oct 12 into Oct 13; Chelsea 3 hit ~4:00 AM IST, Oct 13
items.summary: Drones hit two cargo ships in the Black Sea overnight off Bulgaria, sinking the Guinea-Bissau-flagged HS Dignity near Krapets (5 rescued, 11 sailors missing, search ongoing) and damaging the Maltese-flagged, Ukrainian-operated Chelsea 3 (hit by 3 drones; all 15 crew rescued). PM Rumen Radev said the outcome 'benefits the Russian Federation' without formally accusing Moscow, summoned the Russian ambassador, and phoned NATO chief Rutte and EC president von der Leyen seeking help to bolster maritime/airspace surveillance; Rutte said NATO will adjust its eastern-flank presence 'as needed'. Second such sinking in Bulgaria's waters in a week. (Catch-up: prior runs missed this.) Image: generic tanker stock photo (representative, not the incident).
items.title: Two cargo ships hit by drones off Bulgaria; one sank, 11 sailors missing

items.event_time_ist: evening of Oct 13, 2026 (Kyiv time; night of Oct 13 in IST)
items.summary: Zelensky said Russian ballistic missiles attacked Kyiv late Tuesday evening Oct 13 with the main target energy infrastructure - specifically thermal plant No. 4 (Darnytska CHP-4, which heats and powers Kyiv's Dniprovskyi/Darnytskyi districts and was already badly damaged in February). A separate strike hit a nine-storey apartment block: Mayor Klitschko reported 1 killed and 13 injured (4 serious). Zelensky said there was again 'no advance warning from our partners' - second night running - and cited Ukrainian intelligence that Russia is 'preparing further ballistic missile launches'; he added the facts show Russia does not consider itself bound by Trump's energy ceasefire. Earlier Tuesday Trump denied cutting intel-sharing and, asked about Russian energy strikes, said 'Ukraine hit many sites the day before.'
items.title: Russian ballistic missiles hit Kyiv Tuesday evening, targeting thermal plant No. 4; high-rise hit, 1 killed, 13 injured

items.event_time_ist: Tuesday Oct 13, 2026 (Kyiv); published/updated Tuesday evening US time
items.title: Zelensky confirms to NPR that Trump admin threatened to cut off intel-sharing over refinery strikes
items.summary: In a sit-down NPR interview in Kyiv on Tuesday (by Joanna Kakissis), Zelensky said the Trump administration warned it could cut off intelligence-sharing with Ukraine unless Ukrainian forces stop long-range drone strikes on oil refineries inside Russia - putting on the record the threat FT/CNN reported Monday (and Trump denied Tuesday). He refuted Trump's claim that Ukrainian refinery strikes caused the diesel price spike, blaming instead the Iran war and Strait of Hormuz blockage; said lifting sanctions on Russian diesel won't lower US prices 'because the volume is not enough' but would give Moscow more money to spend on the war; said he learned of the 'energy ceasefire' from Trump's Truth Social post 'like you'; and vowed Ukraine will keep hitting Russian energy/logistics targets unless Russia stops attacking Ukrainian energy sites - 'Putin doesn't respond to diplomacy, he understands force.'

items.event_time_ist: Monday Oct 12, 2026 (video link, remarks published on Telegram)
items.title: Zelensky counter-offers a Ukrainian 'diesel deal' at the Warsaw Security Forum
items.summary: Speaking by video link at the Warsaw Security Forum on Monday, Zelensky challenged Trump's Russian diesel arrangement and counter-proposed a Ukrainian 'diesel deal': 'If there are such deals, then why doesn't America conclude a diesel deal with Ukraine? ... We influence whether these ships sail or not, whether these refineries work or not.' He offered to suspend Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil/diesel infrastructure if Washington can guarantee Moscow stops attacking Ukraine's electricity system, and argued the Russian diesel volumes in Trump's deal are too small to meaningfully affect global prices. Kyiv's grid, connected to the European network, could supply cheaper electricity to Europe if protected.

items.event_time_ist: Letter dated Oct 13; reported ~11 AM PDT Oct 13 / ~11:30 PM IST Oct 13
items.title: 12 bipartisan senators urge Trump to rescind Russian diesel deal
items.summary: A bipartisan letter signed by 12 US senators (6 Republicans incl. McConnell, Tillis, Collins, Armstrong, Murkowski, Cornyn + 6 Democrats led by Blumenthal), dated Tuesday Oct 13, urges Trump to rescind the US-Russia diesel deal, calling it 'a gift to our adversary and a betrayal of our Allies' that 'damages American security interests'. The letter also presses Trump to implement sanctions under the recently passed Graham Russia/Iran sanctions act. Sen. Wicker (Senate Armed Services chair) said at the Warsaw Security Forum there is 'not a very high likelihood' the deal takes effect. Escalation from the Oct 11 joint statement by 7 senators.

items.event_time_ist: Oct 13, 2026 (Ignatius column published; exact time unknown)
items.summary: The US and Europe are drafting a joint peace proposal with four pillars: (1) reconstruction of Ukraine + compensation, (2) security guarantees for Kyiv (US/Europe military-response obligations comparable to NATO Article 5 in case of new aggression), (3) a Russia-Ukraine-Europe energy agreement — possible pipeline supplying Europe with revenue sharing between Moscow and Kyiv, plus terms/timelines for lifting sanctions against Russia, and (4) a ceasefire along the line of contact, as incentive for a territorial compromise not fully satisfying either side. The initiative grew out of the Friday Oct 9 six-hour Florida meeting at Witkoff's Shell Bay Golf Club hosted by envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff with Ukrainian officials and UK/France/Germany representatives; there Kushner and Witkoff asked Kyiv to suspend refinery strikes and warned Trump would finalize the diesel deal. Peskov says Moscow has not seen the plan and denies any link between the diesel deal and Russia's position; a European official quoted says 'Putin does not seem to be taking peace seriously.'
items.title: WaPo: US and Europe drafting joint 4-pillar peace plan (energy deal, security guarantees, frontline ceasefire)

items.event_time_ist: Overnight Oct 13 into Oct 14, 2026; alert map 05:30 AM Oct 14 Kyiv time (08:00 AM IST Oct 14)
items.source_name: Euromaidan Press (Threads), corroborated by a Kyiv resident's Facebook report
items.summary: Euromaidan Press's Threads account (posted 7:38 PM PDT Oct 13 / 02:38 UTC Oct 14) reports Russia attacking Ukraine with ballistic missiles and jet drones, hitting Kyiv's Thermal Power Plant 5 (TEC-5), Trypillia TPP and other energy facilities, causing power outages; its live air-raid alert map timestamped 05:30 Oct 14 Kyiv time shows most of central/northern/eastern Ukraine under alert. A Kyiv resident's Facebook post minutes later reports damage to three electrical substations, one thermal power plant and two combined heat-and-power plants amid ongoing strikes. If confirmed, this is the third straight night of strikes on Kyiv-region energy infrastructure (after the Monday-night and Tuesday-evening attacks already in the timeline) - day 3 of Trump's announced 'energy ceasefire'. No news-outlet confirmation found yet (two targeted searches: general overnight-strike and TPP-5/Trypillia-specific). Image is a verified representative Kyiv strike-damage photo, not this specific strike.
items.title: Overnight Oct 13→14: reported new Russian strike wave on Kyiv-region energy plants (TPP-5, Trypillia TPP) - social early-signal, news not yet confirmed
